nodes.title: Round 7 (main's hybrid-pilot judgement, defect 1): what she speaks from a card is the whole item in the lesson language, never cut. The faded-step card no longer prepends the worked-example problem clipped with an ellipsis. The English card carries the problem only when it fits whole; the Hindi/Hinglish card is the gap line alone (the kits' problems are English). She says the problem in her own words from the content lines, and the board (fadeBoard) keeps it. This supersedes census F3's problem-on-every-card for non-English lessons.

Round 7 (judgement defect 2, OWNER-RESET #6/#8): talk about something else (spoken, or the steer:else chip) is noticed, parked with a promise and come back to. It no longer gets the ways-in offer. With an off-kit subject already named, it is parked at once. Otherwise a warm yes and "what about?" (steering, never a break), and the next turn parks what they name; a filler goes back warmly. Asked again within the window, she engages briefly with the parked topic (detour). An explicit ask for another study topic keeps the topic buttons. Kill switch TAXILA_R7_PARK_TOPIC=off restores the ways-in offer.

Round 7 (judgement defect 3, dc-r7-stop-limits): bye and every other goodbye or leaving phrase gets the one stop check-in first, like bas ho gaya. It ends on a second stop within two turns, on the stop chip, or on Pause → End. Inside or right after a safeguarding episode a goodbye is let go at once (the frozen safety behaviour). On the agent lane, the stop check-in is the Director's: the agent never takes a check-in turn and never ends a lesson the Director did not end. Kill switch TAXILA_R7_BYE_CHECKIN=off.

md.decisions:
## dc-r7-brain-card-whole-lesson-lang (2026-11-04, stream A Brain)

The pilot's worst finding: a Hinglish lesson spoke "Rani runs 3 rounds of a rectangular park 50 m long and 30 m wide. How far does… Khaali jagah bharo: 3 × 160 = ___ m", twice. The card text is what she says byte for byte (the lead slot), so a card cannot carry English or a clipped sentence. The trade-off: in Hindi/Hinglish lessons the child no longer sees the problem on the card itself. It is on the board and in her words.

## dc-r7-brain-change-topic-parks (2026-11-04, stream A Brain)

The owner rule of 2026-10-05 answered "kuch aur baat" with a different way into today's idea. The pilot showed the child asked to talk about something ELSE and got a method menu. Main's judgement replaces it with the human move: notice, promise it a slot, come back, and engage briefly on a real push. The Later list (A7) shows the promise and brings it back before the wrap.

## dc-r7-brain-bye-checkin (2026-11-04, stream A Brain)

W2-I treated "bye" as a true goodbye and ended at once. The owner wants one warm check-in on every stop. The check-in has a one-tap stop, so a child who must leave still leaves in one tap. Safeguarding episodes keep the old release, so as not to touch frozen safety behaviour. The agent lane wrapped on "bas ho gaya" with no check-in; that cannot happen now.
